options_presented.title: Clarification
options_presented.involves: Ask the lender for a written breakdown of how they calculated the amount they are demanding: the interest rate and method, any charges, and which of your payments they counted.
options_presented.howWeHelp: We tell you exactly what to ask for, based on your confirmed facts, and show you how to compare their answer with our calculation. (Ready-made letter drafts are coming soon.)
benefits: Often uncovers mistakes or missing payments.
Creates a written record that helps if the dispute continues.
risks: The lender may not reply, or may refuse to put anything in writing.
It does not by itself change what you owe.
needed: Your loan details and the lender's current demand.
A list of your payments with dates.

options_presented.title: Negotiation
options_presented.involves: Try to agree a fair settlement amount or repayment schedule with the lender, recorded in writing.
options_presented.howWeHelp: We show the calculated figures that support your position and what a written agreement should say. (Ready-made letter drafts are coming soon.)
benefits: Avoids the cost and time of formal steps.
risks: Any agreement must be in writing, with a receipt for every payment.
Don't negotiate alone if you feel unsafe.
You may agree to pay more than a court might order.
needed: The calculated balance and the lender's demand.
What you can realistically pay, and when.

options_presented.title: Legal action
options_presented.involves: Formal steps such as a legal notice, or a complaint to the appropriate authority. Going to court needs the right proceeding, court and documents.
options_presented.howWeHelp: We explain the verified legal provisions and organise your facts, calculation and evidence for a lawyer or legal aid. Nothing is ever filed automatically. (Notice and complaint drafts are coming soon.)
benefits: Puts your position on formal record.
May lead to the dispute being decided by a court or authority.
risks: Takes time and may cost money; outcomes are never guaranteed.
Time limits may apply — get advice early.
A lawyer or legal aid should check any notice or complaint before it is sent.
needed: Advice on the right authority or court.

options_presented.title: Legal assistance
options_presented.involves: Get help from a lawyer, or from your District Legal Services Authority, which may provide free legal aid if you are eligible.
options_presented.howWeHelp: We prepare a clear case summary, calculation and document list you can take to your first meeting.
benefits: A professional checks your case and options.
Free legal aid is available to eligible people.
risks: Free legal aid depends on eligibility criteria and your state's income limit.
needed: Proof of identity (show it in person; never share Aadhaar numbers online).

reasons: The lender's exact demand isn't known. Ask for it in writing, with a breakdown.
alerts: If you have received a court summons, a legal notice or any document with a deadline, contact legal aid or a lawyer immediately — deadlines can't wait for the other steps.

action_plan_steps.title: Organise your evidence
action_plan_steps.detail: No documents are uploaded yet. Look for: loan agreement or promissory note; proof of money received; repayment receipts or records; bank / upi statements; messages with the lender (whatsapp, sms); lender's written demand. Missing items don't stop you, but they make your account easier to dispute. Keep originals safe and work from copies.

action_plan_steps.title: Ask the lender for a written breakdown
action_plan_steps.detail: Ask how they reached the amount they demand: the interest rate and method, the dates used, any charges, and every payment of yours they have counted.

action_plan_steps.title: Send it in a way you can prove
action_plan_steps.detail: Use registered post or a written message (such as WhatsApp) and keep a copy and the delivery proof. Stay polite and stick to facts.

action_plan_steps.title: Compare their answer with our calculation
action_plan_steps.detail: Our calculation is between ₹75,736.8 and ₹77,666.67 on 11 Nov 2026, depending on the agreed terms. Check whether they missed any payment, used a higher rate, compounded interest, or added charges.

action_plan_steps.title: Don't sign anything new while the amount is unclear
action_plan_steps.detail: Avoid signing blank papers, new promissory notes or cheques until the amount is clear.

action_plan_steps.title: Keep your case up to date
action_plan_steps.detail: If anything changes — new payments, new demands, new messages — add it in the chat or case summary and recalculate.
